# Every setting

<!-- Generated by tools/settings_doc.py from ninaivu/server/config.py. Do not edit. -->

Settings resolve in this order, later winning: the default, `config.json` in the
index folder, then the `NINAIVU_*` variable. A variable marked *wins* always
beats config.json; any other only fills in what nobody chose in the console.

**Layer**: *household* settings are on the console's Advanced page; *expert*
ones are changed in config.json, by a variable, or on the one page that owns
them; *runtime* ones say how this start was made and are never saved.

## Library

| Setting | Default | Variable | Layer | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `roots` | `[]` | `NINAIVU_ROOTS` (wins) | household | Every library folder Ninaivu indexes. Members can be assigned one of these, or any folder inside one. |
| `active_root` |  | `NINAIVU_ROOT` (wins) | household | The folder the console shows by default. Always one of roots. |
| `new_files_folder` | `'~/Pictures/Ninaivu'` |  | household | Where new files go when the library folder they belong in cannot be written — an NTFS drive on a Mac, which macOS mounts read-only. Edited copies, approved uploads and phone backups land here instead, in the same folder layout, and it joins the library folders on first use so they appear in the gallery. See ninaivu/storage/new_files.py. |
| `follow_symlinks` | `False` |  | expert | Follow symbolic links inside the library. Off: a link that points back up a tree indexes it twice. |
| `index_hidden` | `True` | `NINAIVU_INDEX_HIDDEN` | household | Index media found in hidden files and folders, but hide it by default. Somebody went to the trouble of hiding it. Skipping it entirely loses photographs the household may still want; showing it in the gallery publishes what was deliberately put out of sight. Indexing it as hidden — admin-only, and visible in the console with a reason — is the only reading that respects both. Set False to skip hidden items again. |
| `min_media_bytes` | `61440` | `NINAIVU_MIN_MEDIA_BYTES` | household | Smallest file, in bytes, that counts as a real photo or video. A folder of old media is full of things that are technically images: icons, sprites, email signatures, web-page furniture, thumbnails left behind by other software. They are not anybody's photographs, and they pad the library and the archive with noise. Anything smaller than this is passed over as if it were not media at all. |
| `import_voice_audio_only` | `True` |  | expert | Importing from a drive brings in the household's own recordings and leaves songs and film soundtracks behind. Every song is listened to before it is copied: one that sounds like continuous music is held back on the Import page with the downloads found by name, where it can still be kept. Voice notes, call recordings, speech and anything a phone or a recorder made are always copied. Off, only songs whose names or tags say they are downloads are held back. |
| `import_copy_workers` | `0` |  | household | Files an import copies at once. 0 leaves it to the engine: half the cores, between two and four. 1 copies one file at a time, as before 2.1. More than a few only queue up on a slow source drive. |
| `ignore_dirs` | `['$RECYCLE.BIN', '.Trash', '.cache', '.git', '.mediavault', '.ninaivu', '.svn', '@eaDir', 'System Volume Information', '__pycache__', '_deleted', 'node_modules']` |  | household | Directory names skipped during a scan. |
| `watch` | `True` | `NINAIVU_WATCH` | expert | Watch the library for changes and index incrementally. |
| `rescan_on_change` | `True` |  | expert | Re-check files whose size or mtime changed. |
| `boot_scan_after` | `900.0` |  | household | Seconds. If the watcher is on and a scan finished this recently, start-up does not walk the library again — that gap is a restart, not a day away. Zero always scans. |
| `watch_debounce` | `2.0` |  | household | Seconds a folder must stay quiet after a change before it is re-read. |
| `bin_erase_after_days` | `0.0` |  | household | Days after which a file in the recycle bin is erased for good. Zero — the default — keeps everything until somebody says otherwise, which is what a bin is for. |
| `hide_screens` | `True` | `NINAIVU_HIDE_SCREENS` | household | Hide screenshots, documents and photographs of screens from everyone but administrators (media/screens.py). By name on every install; by picture once the search model has looked at it. |
| `duplicate_distance` | `6` |  | household | Hamming distance under which two pHashes count as near-duplicates. |
| `quality_scan` | `True` |  | expert | Measure focus and exposure while scanning. Cheap: one 256px greyscale pass over a thumbnail Ninaivu has already decoded. |
| `occasion_scan` | `True` |  | expert | Group the library into occasions after each scan. Metadata only — no pixels are read and no model is loaded, so this runs in every AI tier. |
| `southern_hemisphere` | `False` |  | expert | Which half of the world the seasons in those phrases belong to. June is summer in Atlanta and winter in Adelaide, and a search engine that assumes one of them is wrong for half its households. |
| `date_phrase_search` | `True` |  | expert | Read a date range out of what somebody typed — "last summer", "may 2019", "last week" — and narrow the search with it. |
| `phrase_search` | `True` |  | expert | Read people, places, "videos" and "favourites" out of it too — "Maya and Arjun at Ooty videos" (ninaivu/utils/phrase.py). Only names and places the person searching can already see are ever matched. |
| `xmp_sidecars` | `False` |  | household | Write what the household told Ninaivu — people, albums, favourites, stars, corrected dates, places — beside each photograph as an XMP sidecar (IMG_1.jpg.xmp) other photo programs read (ninaivu/storage/xmp.py). Off: it puts files in the library folders. |
| `house_name` |  | `NINAIVU_HOUSE_NAME` | household | What the household calls this library. The admin sets it once and it is what everyone sees; each family member may then keep their own name for it instead. Empty means "Ninaivu". |

## People

| Setting | Default | Variable | Layer | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open_browsing` | `True` | `NINAIVU_OPEN_BROWSING` | household | Let anyone who reaches the server browse public media without signing in. Family and admin features still require a login. Admins can turn this off to make the whole library private. |
| `lock_after_minutes` | `15` | `NINAIVU_LOCK_AFTER_MINUTES` | household | Cover the screen after this many minutes with nobody there, in both the family app and the console, until the person unlocks it with their password or PIN. Nobody is signed out and nothing in progress stops. 0 turns the lock off. See the screen lock in ninaivu/server/auth.py. |
| `nsfw_filter` | `True` | `NINAIVU_NSFW_FILTER` | household | Flag adult content as explicit: admins only, reviewed on the console's Folders screen. Screenshots and documents are hidden, never explicit. |
| `phone_backup_trusted` | `False` |  | household | Put family members' phone backups straight into the library instead of the review queue. Off by default: a family upload waits for an administrator, and a backup is an upload. An administrator's own phone is always filed straight away. |
| `phone_upload_max_gb` | `8` |  | household | Largest file a phone's sync app may send to the phone inbox (/dav/), in gigabytes. The app sends a file whole, so the web server holds it until it has all arrived; the backup page sends pieces and is not limited by this. Eight is about eighteen minutes of a phone's 4K video. |
| `upload_quota_gb` | `50` |  | household | The most one family member may have waiting for an administrator's approval, in gigabytes: uploads, phone backups, scanned prints and saved edits together. More is refused until some of it is approved or turned away, so one profile (or a phone signed in to it) cannot fill the disk. Zero means no limit. Administrators are not held to it. |
| `lock_roots` | `False` | `NINAIVU_LOCK_ROOTS` | expert | Confine the folder picker to roots and nothing else. Off by default: the picker is behind an admin sign-in, and an admin who cannot reach their own Pictures folder cannot set the library up. Turn it on with --lock-roots when the console is exposed beyond your machine. |
| `first_day_done` | `False` |  | expert | Whether the first-day walk-through in the console has been finished (or skipped). It opens once, right after the administrator is made, and never again once this is set. |
| `home_lat` |  |  | household | The home zone's centre, latitude. Photographs taken inside the zone leave Ninaivu without their location (see strip_location). None: no zone. |
| `home_lon` |  |  | household | The home zone's centre, longitude. |
| `home_radius_m` | `300` |  | household | The home zone's radius, in metres. |
| `strip_location` | `'home'` |  | household | Which files family members open or download without their location: off, home (taken in the home zone) or all. Administrators always get the original; guests and shared links never get a location. |
| `photo_frame` | `True` |  | expert | The living photo frame: a tablet or a TV's browser, signed in, opens Ninaivu at /#frame and drifts through the library full screen, this day in past years first, with when, where, who and the start of any story told about each photograph. See ninaivu/features/frame/media.py. |
| `time_capsules` | `True` |  | expert | Time capsules: photographs and a letter sealed for somebody in the family until a date. Nobody sees inside before then, not even whoever sealed it. See ninaivu/features/capsules/storage.py. |
| `ask_ninaivu` | `True` | `NINAIVU_ASK` | expert | Ask Ninaivu: questions about the family's photographs, in Tamil or English, answered on this computer from what the library already knows (people, places, dates, descriptions, words in photos and stories), with the photographs the answer comes from. Writes its answers with the on-device writing model when it is downloaded, and plainly without it. Nothing is sent anywhere. See ninaivu/ask. |

## Backup

| Setting | Default | Variable | Layer | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cloud_enabled` | `False` | `NINAIVU_CLOUD` | household | Copy the library up to Google Drive, one way, in the background. Off until somebody turns it on, and it stays a copy: nothing in Drive can change, move or remove anything here. Deleting a photograph from Drive does not delete it from the library and does not cause it to be uploaded again — the record of what has gone up is kept here and is never cleared by anything the cloud does. |
| `cloud_folder_name` | `'Ninaivu'` | `NINAIVU_CLOUD_FOLDER` | household | The single Drive folder Ninaivu owns. Everything it uploads goes inside this folder, and it touches nothing else in the account. |
| `cloud_autostart` | `False` | `NINAIVU_CLOUD_AUTOSTART` | household | Start uploading by itself when the server starts. Off by default: a household on a metered connection chooses when the upload begins. |
| `cloud_rate_kbps` | `0` | `NINAIVU_CLOUD_RATE_KBPS` | household | Ceiling on the upload, in kilobytes per second. Zero means no limit, which is the default because a limit nobody chose is its own surprise — but one file at a time is not a cap, and on a slow or metered line the difference matters. Applied between chunks, so it takes effect on a running upload without restarting it. |
| `cloud_window_start` |  | `NINAIVU_CLOUD_WINDOW_START` | household | The hours uploading may run, in local time, as HH:MM. Both empty means any time. A start later than the end crosses midnight, which is the case this is for: 22:00 to 07:00 is "overnight". An upload caught by the closing time stops where it is and resumes the next night. |
| `cloud_window_end` |  | `NINAIVU_CLOUD_WINDOW_END` | household | When the backup's allowed hours end (HH:MM); empty means any time. |
| `cloud_parallel` | `3` |  | household | How many files the backup sends at once. Each waits about two seconds on Google before any of it moves, so one at a time a library of photographs used a third of a 32 Mbit/s line. 1 is one at a time. |
| `cloud_full_speed` | `False` |  | household | Keep uploading at full speed while people use Ninaivu at home, whatever the workload mode says for background work: the backup does not make way for the household, and sends in its larger pieces. It still makes way for anybody using Ninaivu from outside the house, whose photographs come up the same internet connection. The upload hours and the speed cap above still apply. |
| `cloud_encrypt` | `True` |  | household | Encrypt files before they go to Drive, with the key in cloud-encryption.json (made once on the Mugil page). On by default, and nothing is uploaded until the key exists: the promise is that a photograph leaves the house encrypted, and a default of off meant the first backups — and the copy of the index, with everybody's names — went up in the clear. An administrator can still turn it off. |
| `cloud_hidden` | `'never'` |  | household | Whether hidden things are backed up too: "never" (the default: what the household hid does not leave the house), "encrypted" (only while the backup is encrypted), or "always". Hidden includes every sound file — call recordings, voice notes — and the screenshots and documents Ninaivu hides by itself, so with "never" those have no copy in Drive. |
| `cloud_kinds` | `'all'` |  | household | What the household chose to leave out of the backup (ninaivu/cloud/rules.py). Kinds: "all", "no_video" or "pictures". |
| `cloud_max_mb` | `0` |  | household | Nothing larger than this many megabytes goes up. 0 is no limit. |
| `cloud_approval_mb` | `1024` |  | household | Files larger than this (megabytes) are not uploaded to the cloud until an administrator approves each one on the Mugil page — cloud storage is paid for by the gigabyte (ninaivu/cloud/approvals.py). 0: none need it. |
| `cloud_skip_folders` | `[]` |  | household | Folders of the library — paths inside a library folder — that are not backed up, nor anything in them. |
| `cloud_skip_words` | `[]` |  | household | A file with any of these in its name or path is not backed up. |
| `restore_test_days` | `7` |  | household | Restore a few random files from the backup this often, in days, and check them against the originals (ninaivu/cloud/restore_test.py). 0 is off. |
| `restore_test_files` | `5` |  | household | How many files each test restores, and the largest it will pick. |
| `restore_test_max_mb` | `1024` |  | household | The largest file the weekly restore test will bring back to check. |
| `cloud_index_every_hours` | `24` |  | household | Send a copy of the index (faces, albums, visibility, full paths — no secrets) to Drive at most this often, in hours, when it has changed. 0 turns it off. See ninaivu/cloud/index_copy.py. |
| `mirror_enabled` | `False` |  | household | Keep a second, plain copy of the library in a folder on another disk (ninaivu/storage/mirror.py). |
| `mirror_dir` |  |  | household | The folder the second copy is kept in: on another disk, never inside the library or the state folder. |
| `mirror_every_hours` | `24` |  | household | How often Ninaivu brings the second copy up to date by itself, in hours (0: only when asked). An unplugged disk is caught up when it returns. |
| `mirror_verify_days` | `30` |  | household | Read the whole second copy back and compare every fingerprint this often, in days. 0 is only when asked. |
| `offsite_enabled` | `False` |  | household | An encrypted copy somewhere else — any S3-compatible service, or a folder on a share or somebody else's disk (ninaivu/cloud/offsite.py). The secret key is kept apart, owner-only, in the state folder. |
| `offsite_kind` | `'folder'` |  | household | folder or s3. |
| `offsite_folder` |  |  | household | The folder, for folder: a mounted share or another house's disk. |
| `offsite_endpoint` |  |  | household | The S3-compatible service's address, e.g. https://s3.eu-central-003.backblazeb2.com |
| `offsite_region` | `'us-east-1'` |  | household | The service's region, as it names it. |
| `offsite_bucket` |  |  | household | The bucket the off-site copy goes in. |
| `offsite_prefix` | `'ninaivu'` |  | household | The folder inside the bucket. |
| `offsite_access_key` |  |  | household | The service's access key id (the secret key is kept apart, never here). |
| `offsite_every_hours` | `24` |  | household | How often the off-site copy is brought up to date, in hours. |
| `scrub_every_days` | `30` |  | household | How often the storage check reads every file of the library and compares it with its fingerprint, by itself, starting in the small hours (ninaivu/storage/repair.py). 0 leaves it to the button. |
| `scrub_repair` | `True` |  | household | Put back what that check finds damaged or missing, from the second copy or Drive — only ever from a copy whose bytes match what the file was. |
| `backup_every_hours` | `24.0` |  | household | The index is the one thing the library itself does not carry: names, albums, visibility, share links, corrected dates. Hours between snapshots; zero turns it off. They land in the state directory unless `backup_dir` says otherwise — put that on another disk if you have one. |
| `backup_keep` | `7` | `NINAIVU_BACKUP_KEEP` | household | How many dated copies of the index to keep on this computer. |
| `backup_dir` |  | `NINAIVU_BACKUP_DIR` (wins) | household | Where the copies of the index go; empty means inside the state folder. Not inside a library folder or the second copy. Outside the state folder, the copies leave out the cloud key and the Google sign-in. |
| `keepsake_letter` |  |  | household | The letter written into the family archive on a USB drive (ninaivu/storage/keepsake.py), for whoever opens it. |
| `keepsake_folder` |  |  | household | The drive or folder the family archive was last made in. |
| `keepsake_made` | `0` |  | household | When the family archive was last made whole (seconds since 1970; 0 for never). |
| `mugil_role` | `'single'` |  | household | single (everything on this computer, as always), primary (this computer runs the library and sends its originals to the Secondary) or secondary (this computer keeps the originals it is sent). |
| `mugil_partner_url` |  |  | household | On the Primary: the Secondary's console address, e.g. http://linux-pc:3000. |
| `mugil_originals_dir` |  |  | household | On the Secondary: the folder the originals are kept in, on the big disk. |
| `mugil_copy_every_hours` | `24` |  | household | On the Primary: how often the originals are sent by themselves, in hours (0: only when asked). |
| `mugil_family_copy` | `False` |  | household | On the Primary: also send the family app's read-only copy (the index, thumbnails, faces) to the Secondary, so the family can browse there while this computer is off (mugil/handover.py). |
| `mugil_free_space` | `False` |  | household | Not used since 4.0.1, and always off: the Primary no longer lets originals go (mugil/free.py). Kept so that a settings file from 4.0.0 that has it still loads. |
| `mugil_copy_mode` | `'automatic'` |  | household | On the Secondary: how the originals first arrive. automatic: the Primary sends every one of them once the two are paired. manual: the household copies the library folder onto the disk by hand, and the Primary waits until it is said to be done and checked here, then sends only what is missing or different (mugil/adopt.py). |

## Remote access

| Setting | Default | Variable | Layer | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `network_access` | `True` |  | household | The Network access switch on the console's Server page. Off, Ninaivu answers only on this computer - the family app and the console both bind to 127.0.0.1 and no name is announced - however it was started: an explicit --host 0.0.0.0 from start.py or the desktop panel does not override it. On, host and --local-only decide as before. |
| `https` |  |  | household | The "Use HTTPS" switch on the console's Server page: "on" or "off". Empty until the first start decides (server/https_choice.py): HTTP for a new install, HTTPS kept for one that has served it before. |
| `console_on_network` | `False` |  | household | Let other devices at home open the console too. Off by default: the console is where the library is run, and on a new install it is where the administrator is made, so it answers on this computer only until somebody decides otherwise on the Server page. --admin-host (or NINAIVU_ADMIN_HOST) still sets the address outright. |
| `console_from_internet` | `False` |  | household | Let the console open from the internet: through a public tunnel or proxy, or from a public address. Off by default, and best left off — the console is where the library is run, and from away it is reached over Tailscale or WireGuard, which this never blocks. |
| `tailnet_https` | `True` |  | household | Answer this computer's Tailscale name (<computer>.<tailnet>.ts.net) with the certificate Tailscale gives it, so the household's devices on the tailnet reach Ninaivu from anywhere without a certificate warning (ninaivu/utils/tailnet.py). Does nothing without Tailscale, or until the tailnet owner turns HTTPS certificates on. |
| `remote_access` | `'auto'` |  | household | How the household reaches Ninaivu from outside the house: "auto" (Tailscale if it is on this machine, else none), "tailscale", "wireguard", "tunnel", "proxy" or "none". See ninaivu/server/remote.py for what each one changes. |
| `remote_networks` | `[]` |  | household | For "wireguard": the tunnel's address ranges ("10.8.0.0/24"), which nothing can tell from the LAN without being told. |
| `remote_hostname` |  |  | household | For "tunnel" and "proxy": the public name that reaches Ninaivu, listed on the Server page for the household. Ninaivu answers to it. |
| `allowed_hosts` | `[]` |  | household | Public names Ninaivu answers to besides the ones a home network uses (addresses, .local, .lan, dotless names, .ts.net). A name a tunnel or a reverse proxy gives it goes here — photos.example.org, or .example.org for every name under it. Anything else is refused, which is what stops a website pointing its own domain at this computer (DNS rebinding) and reading the library. See ninaivu/server/hosts.py. |
| `notify_webhook` |  | `NINAIVU_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK` | household | Off unless one of these is set. Nothing phones anywhere by default. |
| `notify_webhook_format` | `'json'` |  | household | Shape of the webhook body: json (also read by Slack and Discord), ntfy or form. |
| `notify_smtp_host` |  | `NINAIVU_NOTIFY_SMTP_HOST` | household | Mail server for notifications; empty means no email. |
| `notify_smtp_port` | `587` |  | household | Mail server port. |
| `notify_smtp_user` |  |  | household | Mail server sign-in name. |
| `notify_smtp_password` |  |  | household | Mail server password. Kept in config.json readable by this account only. |
| `notify_smtp_to` |  | `NINAIVU_NOTIFY_SMTP_TO` | household | Who notification emails go to. |
| `notify_smtp_tls` | `True` |  | household | Use STARTTLS when talking to the mail server (port 465 is always TLS). Off, a mail password is sent only to a relay on this computer. |
| `notify_events` | `[]` |  | household | Which events are sent; empty means all of them. |
| `notify_quiet_seconds` | `21600` |  | household | The same event is not sent again within this many seconds. |
| `digest_enabled` | `False` |  | household | One photograph from this day in a past year, sent to the family. Off by default, and it borrows the mail server above rather than asking for it twice — but nothing else. Alerts go to whoever looks after the machine; photographs go to the household, which is a different list of people and a different promise about what may be put in a message. See `ninaivu/utils/digest.py`. |
| `digest_to` |  |  | household | Who it goes to. Comma-separated; empty means nobody, which is off. |
| `digest_weekday` | `6` |  | household | Monday is 0, as `datetime.weekday()` counts. Sunday morning by default: the time a household is most likely to have a minute for it. |
| `digest_hour` | `9` |  | household | Hour of the day (0–23) the weekly digest is sent. |
| `digest_link` |  |  | household | Where "see the rest" points. A home server is only reachable from the house, so this is offered rather than assumed. |
| `tv_album` | `0` |  | household | The one album the televisions at home may show, by its number; 0 is off, which is the default. Ninaivu then answers as a DLNA media server (what a TV's own media player, VLC and Kodi look for), on the home network only and with nobody signed in, so it offers this album and nothing else: never a hidden or flagged photograph, a sound recording or anything in the bin, even when the album holds one. See ninaivu/server/tv_album.py. |
| `tv_port` | `8200` |  | household | The port the TV album answers on. 8200 is what home media servers commonly use; it only matters if another program already has it. |

## AI

| Setting | Default | Variable | Layer | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ai_enabled` | `True` | `NINAIVU_AI` | household | Run the AI passes at all (tagging, search, descriptions). Off leaves the gallery, faces and places working. |
| `ai_engine` | `'auto'` | `NINAIVU_AI_ENGINE` | household | "auto" picks CLIP when torch is importable, else the light tagger. |
| `hardware_tier` | `'auto'` |  | household | Which kind of computer this is treated as: auto (measured from the memory and the graphics processor at start), basic (2 GB and no GPU: everything but the large models) or full. Decides what ai_engine = auto means and the defaults of the expensive passes; never turns a switch the household set. See server/tiers.py. |
| `ai_gpu` | `True` | `NINAIVU_AI_GPU` | household | Run the image model on a graphics processor when there is one that works: NVIDIA's (CUDA) or a Mac's own (Metal). Off keeps it on the processor. Takes effect when Ninaivu next starts. |
| `ai_image_device` | `'auto'` | `NINAIVU_AI_IMAGE_DEVICE` | household | Where the on-device AI engine (ai_runtime) runs its image models: auto, cpu (the processor), coreml (a Mac's Neural Engine and graphics processor) or coreml-gpu (its graphics processor only). auto is Core ML for search on a Mac with Apple silicon, where an M4 Pro analysed photographs ten times faster than on the processor, and the processor for the description and colouring models until they are measured; the best graphics card there is elsewhere. Core ML compiles a model once, a minute or two, and keeps it. Off (ai_gpu) means the processor whatever this says. Takes effect when Ninaivu next starts. |
| `clip_model` | `'auto'` |  | household | "auto": SigLIP 2 once downloaded (Admin → AI models), else ViT-B-32. |
| `clip_pretrained` | `'laion2b_s34b_b79k'` |  | household | Which weights of the CLIP model to use. |
| `clip_batch_size` | `16` |  | household | Photographs handed to the model at once; lower on a small machine. |
| `tag_threshold` | `0.18` |  | household | Minimum cosine similarity for a zero-shot tag to be kept. |
| `max_tags` | `8` |  | household | The most tags kept per photograph. |
| `nsfw_threshold` | `0.6` |  | household | How sure the screen must be before a photograph is held back as explicit (0–1). |
| `underwear_threshold` | `0.005` |  | household | How much a picture must look like people in only their underwear before it is flagged explicit too (media/revealing.py; SigLIP 2's scale, 0–1). Measured on a family library of 153,765 pictures: 0.005 flags 1,292, 0.02 flags 328 and 0.05 only 130. 0 turns the check off. |
| `explicit_threshold` | `0.005` |  | household | The explicit check's line on SigLIP 2's scale (sigmoid probabilities), where nsfw_threshold above is CLIP's. 0.01 until 2026-10-26, when a family library had about 3,900 photos and videos scored between 0.005 and 0.01 still shown to the family; the household asked that family members see only clean content. |
| `faces_enabled` | `False` | `NINAIVU_FACES` | household | Detect and group faces. Off unless the models have been fetched, and independent of the AI tier: face grouping is OpenCV, not CLIP, so it works on a machine with no torch at all. |
| `face_model` | `'sface'` | `NINAIVU_FACE_MODEL` | household | Which pair of models finds faces and tells people apart: sface (OpenCV's YuNet and SFace, the default, Apache-2.0) or arcface (InsightFace's SCRFD and ArcFace, downloaded from the AI models page; better at relatives and at a child over the years; their licence allows non-commercial use only). Switching has the next scan look at every photograph again; names already confirmed are kept by position. |
| `place_names` | `False` |  | household | Turn the coordinates a camera recorded into the name of a place, so an occasion can be called "Ooty, 12–14 May 2023" rather than a date alone. Off by default because turning it on fetches a gazetteer once — about 11 MB from GeoNames. That request is the only one: after it, every lookup is arithmetic on a table in the state directory, and no coordinate of yours is ever sent anywhere. |
| `place_max_km` | `50.0` |  | household | Further than this from the nearest known place and the photograph is left unnamed, rather than given a name it has no real claim to. |
| `map_tiles` | `False` |  | household | Draw the map on tiles fetched from OpenStreetMap instead of the outline Ninaivu ships. Off by default, and this is the one setting in Ninaivu that decides whether anything about your photographs leaves the machine. A tile server is sent the square of the world you are looking at, one request per tile: open the map on last summer's holiday and somebody else's logs know where your family spent it, and roughly when you looked. With it off the map is drawn from `static/data/world.geojson`, a coastline-and-borders outline of the whole world that ships in the repository. It shows which country and which coast, which is what a map of a family library is usually being asked; it does not show streets. Turning this on trades that privacy for streets, knowingly. |
| `ocr_enabled` | `False` |  | household | Read the words in photographs — signs, menus, screenshots, the back of a postcard — and make them searchable. Off by default: it needs the optional OCR package (see requirements-ocr.txt), and it is a second or so per photograph the first time through a library. Like faces, this is a capability rather than an AI tier: it answers a different question from tagging and is turned on separately. |
| `ocr_min_score` | `0.5` |  | household | Below this the reader is guessing. Foliage, brickwork and carpet all produce confident-looking nonsense, and one wrong line in the index is worse than a missing one. |
| `ocr_max_chars` | `4000` |  | household | Characters kept per photograph. A scan of a newspaper page would otherwise put a whole article into a column meant for a shop sign. |
| `speech_languages` | `'ta,en'` |  | household | The languages the household speaks in its voice stories, as two-letter codes, most used first. A story heard as any other language is taken to be the first one (Whisper sometimes hears Tamil as Malayalam). |
| `video_keyframes` | `5` |  | household | How many moments across a clip to tag, rather than the poster frame alone. A holiday video is a beach, a restaurant and a car park; one frame at the one-second mark describes none of them. Zero or one keeps the old single-frame behaviour. |
| `detect_orientation` | `True` | `NINAIVU_DETECT_ORIENTATION` | expert | Work out which way up a photograph goes when the file does not say. Only ever for files with no usable EXIF orientation — a camera's own tag is never second-guessed. Scanned prints, photographs a messaging app stripped on the way through, anything re-saved by an editor that dropped the tag: those are the cases. Set False to leave every untagged photograph exactly as it sits on disk. |
| `orientation_ai` | `False` | `NINAIVU_ORIENTATION_AI` | expert | Also ask CLIP when the faces found nothing. Off by default. Faces are decisive and nearly free. CLIP is neither: it has to embed all four rotations of a photograph, and the photographs that reach it are the ones with no faces in them — landscapes, mostly, which it has least to say about. On a fifty-thousand-item library that is minutes of work for a handful of corrections, so it is offered rather than assumed. |
| `straighten_requires_face` | `True` | `NINAIVU_STRAIGHTEN_REQUIRES_FACE` | expert | Only ever straighten a photograph with a person in it. The orientation model is happy to judge a landscape, a document or a plate of food, and it is usually right — but "usually" is not the bar for rewriting somebody's library unattended. A found face is a second, independent witness that the picture is of people and that this way up is the way a person stands. Off, it will straighten everything it is confident about. |
| `straighten_auto` | `True` | `NINAIVU_STRAIGHTEN_AUTO` | expert | Look for sideways photographs by itself, after every scan. On, the survey runs over whatever a scan has just indexed (and only that — what it has already looked at is remembered), and what it finds waits on Review → Straighten for a person to approve, unless straighten_auto_apply is on. This only decides whether somebody has to remember to press the button. Off, the button is the only way. |
| `straighten_auto_apply` | `True` | `NINAIVU_STRAIGHTEN_AUTO_APPLY` | expert | Turn what that automatic survey finds, without waiting for approval. The survey only proposes what the model is sure of (and, by default, only photographs with a person in them), and each run is one batch that Undo puts back exactly, thumbnails included. A survey started by the button is never applied for you: somebody who pressed it is there to look. |
| `ai_models_dir` |  | `NINAIVU_AI_MODELS_DIR` (wins) | household | Where every AI model lives — the search model, the editing models, the face detector and recogniser, the orientation model. Empty means the `.ai-models` folder beside the application in a checkout, and a folder of the person's own for an installed copy (model_catalog.user_models_dir), which upgrades never replace. One folder on purpose: moving Ninaivu to another machine is then this, the state folder and the library, and nothing else to hunt for. |
| `extensions` | `[]` |  | household | The extensions switched on, by name (see ninaivu/extensions.py). Every extension is off until an administrator turns it on in the console, and a change takes effect at the next start. Empty by default, always. |
| `outside_ai_for_family` | `False` |  | household | Let family members use extensions that send a photograph out of the house (Gemini). Off: turning such an extension on is the administrator's decision, and so is each photograph it sends. |
| `ai_server_url` |  |  | household | A ComfyUI instance on another machine in the house, for image edits the Ninaivu machine is too small to run. Off until an administrator sets the address in the console; photographs go to that address and nowhere else. |
| `ai_server_enabled` | `False` |  | household | Hand heavy edits to the AI server named in ai_server_url. |
| `ai_server_edit_workflow` |  |  | household | Workflow (by its id in the console) that serves each Playground job; empty leaves that job on the local model, as before. |
| `ai_server_remove_workflow` |  |  | household | ComfyUI workflow file for object removal; empty uses the built-in one. |
| `ai_server_upscale_workflow` |  |  | household | ComfyUI workflow file for upscaling; empty uses the built-in one. |
| `ai_server_restore_workflow` |  |  | household | ComfyUI workflow file for photo restoration; empty uses the built-in one. |
| `ai_server_colorize_workflow` |  |  | household | ComfyUI workflow file for colourising; empty uses the built-in one. |
| `ai_server_inpaint_workflow` |  |  | household | The workflow that redraws a painted area to a request (Sudar's Add hair). |
| `ai_server_timeout` | `180` |  | household | Seconds to wait for one job, queue time included. |
| `ai_server_max_side` | `1024` |  | household | Longest side of the preview the Playground sends for a server job. |

Each part works once its pieces are there; nothing is downloaded until asked for. Search moves to the engine at the next start. Off: nothing of it runs. |

| `life_story` | `True` | `NINAIVU_LIFE_STORY` | expert | A life in photographs: one person's life told decade by decade, from their page or the Create menu: each chapter the best photographs of those years, where they were, who was beside them and who joined their photographs for the first time, the trips, and the stories the family told, their own voice first. A short title and a few sentences for each chapter by the on-device writing model when it is downloaded, kept for next time; plain words without it. Counted on this computer from what the library already knows; nothing is sent anywhere. See ninaivu/features/life_story/media.py. |
| `festival_albums` | `True` | `NINAIVU_FESTIVAL_ALBUMS` | expert | Festival albums: every Deepavali, every Pongal, Karthigai Deepam, Navaratri's golu and the rest, found without anybody tagging. Nothing is sent anywhere. See ninaivu/features/festivals/media.py. |
| `letters_aloud` | `False` | `NINAIVU_LETTERS_ALOUD` | expert | Letters read aloud: an old letter, a recipe card or a note in a grandparent's hand, photographed, is given its words, written out under it (read by the text reader, or typed and corrected by the family) and read aloud in a calm Tamil or English voice, from Read aloud in the viewer. A memory film narrates a letter with that reading when nobody recorded a story about it. The voices are Meta's MMS models from the AI models page, never anybody's own voice. | `young_faces` | `False` | `NINAIVU_YOUNG_FACES` | expert | Young faces, older names: who an unnamed child in an old photograph may be, from the faces the family has named in later years, the year each person was born and the family tree. | `easy_view` | `False` | `NINAIVU_EASY_VIEW` | expert | Easy view: for a grandparent, the family app with bigger photographs and words, fewer buttons, and each photograph told aloud in Tamil or English: who the family named in it, where and when it was taken and how long ago that was, and a caption the family wrote. Turned on per profile, by the person in their profile or by an administrator on the console's People page. | `photo_talk` | `True` | `NINAIVU_PHOTO_TALK` | expert | Talk about this photo: ask the photograph open in the viewer a question ("what does the banner say?", "which temple is this?") and the on-device writing model looks at it and answers in a few sentences, in Tamil or English. See ninaivu/features/photo_talk/media.py. |
| `find_print` | `True` | `NINAIVU_FIND_PRINT` | expert | Find this print: photograph a framed print or a page of an album with the family app (Add photos menu) and Ninaivu finds the photograph it is a copy of, by the picture fingerprint every photograph keeps and by the picture search, or says it has no copy yet and takes the print in as a scanned print. Compared on this computer; the phone's picture is sent nowhere. See ninaivu/features/find_print/media.py. |
| `photo_stacks` | `True` | `NINAIVU_PHOTO_STACKS` | expert | Photo stacks: the frames of a burst, and a photograph with the copies edited from it, are one tile in the timeline, with how many there are on it; the sharpest is on top unless somebody chose another, and the viewer shows the rest beside it. | `share_blur_strangers` | `False` | `NINAIVU_SHARE_BLUR_STRANGERS` | expert | Share without strangers: on every share link, the faces nobody in the household has named are blurred: the photograph, its browser copy and its tiles. Videos are shared as they are. On this computer; nothing is sent anywhere. See ninaivu/media/share_faces.py. |
| `voice_search` | `True` | `NINAIVU_VOICE_SEARCH` | expert | Search by speaking: a microphone in the search box. The recording is read and thrown away; nothing is kept and nothing is sent anywhere. The browser allows the microphone only over the secure (https) address. |
| `colour_photos` | `True` | `NINAIVU_COLOUR_PHOTOS` | expert | Colour for black-and-white photographs: "Add colour" in the viewer of a photograph that has none, by the colouring model (DDColor, AI models page) on this computer. The result is shown beside the original to compare and kept, if wanted, as a copy beside it, as an edit is; the original is never changed. The copy can be compared with its original at any time afterwards. |

| `thumb_quality` | `82` |  | expert | Thumbnail compression quality (1–100). |

| `perceptual_hash` | `True` |  | expert | Compute perceptual hashes for duplicate detection. |
| `blur_threshold` | `45.0` |  | expert | Laplacian variance below which a photograph reads as soft. Measured at a fixed size (see media.QUALITY_EDGE) so one number holds across cameras. Deliberately low — a wrongly flagged keeper is worse than a soft frame that slips through. |
| `dark_threshold` | `0.16` |  | expert | Mean luma, 0-1. Below the first is underexposed, above the second is washed out. |
| `bright_threshold` | `0.86` |  | expert | Mean brightness above which a photograph counts as blown out (0–1). |
| `highlight_clip_threshold` | `0.12` |  | expert | Fraction of pixels at the top of the range before highlights count as blown. |
| `low_res_pixels` | `307200` |  | expert | Pixel count below which a still is flagged as low resolution. |
| `occasion_gap_hours` | `6.0` |  | expert | A silence longer than this ends one occasion and starts the next. Six hours keeps a day out and the evening that followed it together, and still separates two consecutive days. |
| `occasion_radius_km` | `60.0` |  | expert | Kilometres. A jump further than this between two photographs that both carry coordinates also ends an occasion. Zero groups on time alone. |
| `occasion_min_items` | `4` |  | expert | Runs shorter than this are not occasions, just stray frames. |
| `content_fingerprints` | `True` | `NINAIVU_CONTENT_FINGERPRINTS` | expert | Keep a fingerprint of every file's contents (BLAKE3), so a photograph moved or renamed in Finder or Explorer keeps its faces, stories, albums and edits, and exact copies are found across every library folder. Filling them in reads every file once, after a scan's other work, and carries on where it was after a stop. Nothing on disk changes. Off: as in 1.12, a moved file is indexed as a new one. |
| `change_journal` | `True` | `NINAIVU_CHANGE_JOURNAL` | expert | Keep a journal of what changes in the library: every file added, edited, renamed, moved, put in the bin or removed, with when. The console's Library changes shows it a day at a time and warns when hundreds of files go or are written over in one folder at once; on a Mac, start-up reads only the folders the drive says changed while Ninaivu was not running. Kept a year. Off: nothing is written down. |
| `proxy_cache_mb` | `4096` | `NINAIVU_PROXY_CACHE_MB` | expert | Ceiling for the folder of converted videos, in megabytes. They are derivatives, so losing them costs only the time to make them again. |
| `workload_mode` | `'balanced'` |  | expert | How background work — indexing, analysis, uploads, storage checks — shares the machine with people using Ninaivu. balanced gives way to video playback; quiet waits whenever anyone is using the app; overnight keeps the heavy work for the night hours below and runs it flat out then; maintenance gives the whole computer to the administrators' work and shows the family app's members a downtime notice. See ninaivu/server/workload.py. |
| `maintenance_before` | `[]` |  | expert | While Maintenance mode is on: the mode and Tuning profile it put aside, and when it began, so leaving it puts them back. Empty otherwise. |
| `workload_night_start` | `'23:00'` |  | expert | The night, for overnight, as local HH:MM. Crosses midnight. |
| `workload_night_end` | `'06:00'` |  | expert | When overnight mode's night ends (HH:MM). |
| `daily_catchup` | `False` | `NINAIVU_DAILY_CATCHUP` | expert | The daily catch-up (new in 2.0, a trial): the heavy analysis (tags, faces, words in photographs, descriptions, voice stories, fingerprints, video and the straightening survey) waits for one stretch of the day and runs then only while the computer is idle: nobody using the app for five minutes, no video playing, and other programs using under 15% of the processor for three minutes. It stops when somebody opens the app or the computer gets busy, and carries on the next day where it got to. New photographs still appear straight away. The computer must be awake at that time: Ninaivu cannot wake it. Off: analysis follows the Background work choice. |
| `daily_catchup_at` | `'02:00'` |  | expert | When the daily catch-up's stretch begins, local HH:MM. |
| `daily_catchup_hours` | `6` |  | expert | How many hours the daily catch-up's stretch lasts (24: all day, whenever idle). |
| `tuning_profile` | `'auto'` |  | expert | How hard Ninaivu works this computer: auto (measured at start as a small box, an everyday computer or a powerful one), or small, medium, large or peak (every core and up to 95% of the memory). Set on the console's Tuning page; see server/tuning.py. |
| `tuning` | `[]` |  | expert | Tuning knobs the administrator set outright on the Tuning page, by name. Anything not here is sized from the profile. |
| `page_size` | `200` |  | expert | Page size for the gallery API. |
| `max_page_size` | `1000` |  | expert | The most items one gallery request may ask for. |
| `state_dir` | *(this computer)* | `NINAIVU_STATE_DIR` | runtime | Where Ninaivu keeps its index, thumbnails, models and settings. Set at start (NINAIVU_STATE_DIR). |
| `host` | `'0.0.0.0'` | `NINAIVU_HOST` (wins) | runtime | Which addresses to serve on. 0.0.0.0 means "every address this machine has", which is what makes phones and tablets on the same Wi-Fi able to reach it — the whole point of a family library. Pass --local-only (or set host to 127.0.0.1) to keep it to this machine. |
| `port` | `80` | `NINAIVU_PORT` (wins) | runtime | The family app — the one everyone in the house opens. 80 is the standard HTTP port, so an mDNS name resolves with nothing typed after it (http://ninaivu.local, not http://ninaivu.local:5000). start.py's own --port default is what actually governs a normal launch (it always passes an explicit value through), so this default mainly matters for `python -m ninaivu` run directly. |
| `admin_host` |  | `NINAIVU_ADMIN_HOST` (wins) | runtime | Address the admin console binds to. None means "the same as host", which is today's behaviour and keeps an existing deployment's reachable addresses unchanged on upgrade. Set this to 127.0.0.1 to serve the family app to the whole house while keeping the console reachable only from this machine -- the split the two ports exist for in the first place. main() warns at startup whenever the console ends up bound beyond loopback. |
| `admin_port` | `3000` | `NINAIVU_ADMIN_PORT` (wins) | runtime | The admin console, deliberately on a different port so it can be firewalled off or bound to localhost independently -- set via admin_host below, or --admin-host/NINAIVU_ADMIN_HOST. |
| `debug` | `False` | `NINAIVU_DEBUG` (wins) | runtime | Flask debug mode. Set at start; never in a house. |
| `server_threads` | `8` | `NINAIVU_SERVER_THREADS` (wins) | runtime | Size of the request thread pool. Eight is generous for a household and small enough that the SQLite connection cache stays a cache. |
| `trusted_proxies` | `0` | `NINAIVU_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (wins) | runtime | How many reverse proxies sit in front of Ninaivu, each adding one address to X-Forwarded-For on the way in. Set it to the number of proxies you run — 1 for Caddy, nginx or a Cloudflare tunnel alone — and never higher: Ninaivu counts that many addresses in from the right and believes the one it lands on, so every hop beyond your real proxies is an address the visitor wrote, and the rate limits, "home or the internet" and "this computer" would all be judged by it. Zero — the default — means the client address and the scheme are read from the connection itself, which is right for a machine in the house answering the household directly. Behind nginx or Caddy that address is always 127.0.0.1, which silently collapses the login rate limiter into one shared bucket for the whole world and leaves the session cookie without its Secure flag on an HTTPS site. Setting this to 1 makes Ninaivu read X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto instead, from a proxy on this computer; one elsewhere (another machine, another container) is listed in NINAIVU_TRUSTED_PROXY_ADDRESSES as well. It is off by default because on a directly-exposed port those headers are written by whoever is calling, and trusting them there would let an attacker forge a new address for every attempt and defeat the very limiter this is meant to protect. |
| `max_upload_mb` | `512` | `NINAIVU_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` (wins) | runtime | Ceiling on a single request body, in megabytes. Covers /api/upload -- raise it if the household shoots video larger than this. |
| `index_file` |  |  | runtime | The index file, when it is not index.db in the state folder: the replica serves each hand-over from a file of its own. |
| `replica_from` |  |  | runtime | From the command line: the hand-over folder this process serves a read-only copy from (--replica-of). Empty: not a replica. |
| `replica_primary_url` |  |  | runtime | The Primary's family app address, to send people to while it is awake (--replica-primary). |
| `replica_wake_mac` |  |  | runtime | The Primary's network (MAC) address, to wake it with (--replica-wake). |
